Order 
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of CrPC, 1973) for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.14/2023 registered at Police Station - Bahadurpur District - Ashoknagar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376,
511, 376DA, 376(2) () of IPC and section 17/18, 5G/6 of POCSO Act and section 92 () of The Right of Persons With Disabilities Act, 2016.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Applicant is in detention since 03.10.2023.
The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 08.11.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.41761 of 2024.
The allegation of rape against minor girl is alleged against the present applicant.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that after dismissal of earlier NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:16798 2 MCRC-15401-2025 bail application of the applicant as withdrawn vide order dated 08.11.2024, the present bail application has been filed after receipt of DNA test report and DNA sample of applicant did not match with that of prosecutrix whereas DNA sample of the Santkumar @ Santa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108247504/
1 co-accused who had been extended benefit of bail by this Court vide order dated 19.04.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 52842 of 2023 was found positive.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since last more than one and a half years.
Charge-sheet in the matter has been filed and further custodial interrogation of the applicant is no more required.
Thus, it is prayed that benefit of bail be extended to the petitioner.
In rebuttal, learned counsel for the State submits that DNA profile of the applicant fully matched with that of prosecutrix.
The prosecutrix is minor and mentally retarded.
The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. has supported the case of prosecution and apart from this, the applicant has four criminal cases registered against him.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of present bail application.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
The allegation against the applicant is of committing rape of a minor girl.
The applicant appears to be the main accused.
The statements of the prosecutrix recorded u/s 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. indicate that the same is implicative in nature qua the present applicant.
There is no new circumstance favouring the applicant except the ostensible delay in the trial.

Delay, if any, gets outweighed by the gravity of the offence and,
therefore the ground of delay is of no assistance to the applicant.

This Court, looking to the gravity of offence and the fact that DNA NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:16798 3 MCRC-15401-2025 profile of the applicant matched with the prosecutrix and period of incarceration, which is only more than one and a half years, is not inclined to grant bail and, therefore rejects the present bail application.
Accordingly, this bail application hereby stands dismissed.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE ojha Santkumar @ Santa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108247504/
